change.describe: branch `pr-67876-flat` of sentry-67876-flat against f3b740199ef0b8057c2c68a377fd3b4d42346deb (merge-base f3b7401)
change.title: pr-67876-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: KeyError when the existing Integration has no `sender` in its metadata
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every Integration row has a `sender`. `build_integration` only sets it when `state` has a `sender` (integration.py:376-377). Only the installation webhook passes one (webhook.py:202-209). An Integration created through this pipeline has no `sender`; `test_basic_flow` asserts exactly that metadata (test_integration.py:303-310). `installation.py:44` already guards against a missing `sender`. If an org removes the integration in Sentry, its OrganizationIntegration goes away but the Integration row stays ACTIVE. Reinstalling the same GitHub installation then reaches this line and fails with a 500 instead of an error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and decide on purpose what should happen when the sender is unknown.

findings.title: Network and HTTP errors in the OAuth exchange are not handled and become a 500
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` (line 423) runs outside the `try`, so a connection error or timeout escapes. `get_user_info` calls `resp.raise_for_status()` (identity/github/provider.py:16), so a revoked token or a 401/5xx from `api.github.com/user` raises `HTTPError`, and nothing catches it. In both cases the user gets a server error inside the install popup instead of the `github-integration-failed.html` page, which posts a failure to `window.opener`. Catch these errors and return `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

findings.title: The installer check is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: The new check that the authenticated GitHub user matches the installer only runs when an Integration already exists (lines 493-505). If the installation webhook has not been processed yet, `Integration.DoesNotExist` goes straight to `next_step()`. `build_integration` then fetches the installation with the app's credentials and links it to the current org, and no sender is ever compared. Anyone who knows an `installation_id` before the webhook lands can still claim it. Consider checking the sender from `get_installation_info` (or the webhook state) on this path as well.

findings.title: `redirect_uri` goes into the authorize URL without URL-encoding
findings.body: The authorize URL is built with an f-string, so `redirect_uri` (an absolute URL that contains `:` and `/`) is not encoded. That works today only because the path has no `?`, `&` or `#`. Building the query with `urlencode({...})` would be more robust. The test at test_integration.py:233-236 asserts the exact unencoded string, so it would need updating too.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests a missing installation
findings.body: The test now sends `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which does not match the pipeline signature. The request fails at the state check (integration.py:412-413) and returns the default "Invalid installation request.". It never reaches `build_integration`'s 404 handling (integration.py:354-356), so the 404 stub is unused and the "The GitHub installation could not be found." path has lost its coverage. Send the correct state through the OAuth step and keep asserting the not-found message.

contracts.action: New OAuthLoginView step: redirects to GitHub OAuth authorize, then exchanges the code for a token and reads the user's login
contracts.before_after: The new step stores installation_id from the query in state, checks state against the pipeline signature, then posts the code to the access_token URL and calls get_user_info.
contracts.visible_effect: Invalid state or a missing token or login shows the github-integration-failed page and posts a failure to window.opener.
contracts.failure_mode: safe_urlopen errors and get_user_info's raise_for_status are not caught, so they become a 500.

contracts.action: GitHubInstallation compares the authenticated GitHub login with integration.metadata.sender.login
contracts.before_after: The new code indexes sender without a guard, and only on the path where the Integration exists.
contracts.visible_effect: A mismatch shows the error page.
contracts.failure_mode: A KeyError (500) when the Integration was created by the pipeline, which never stores a sender.

contracts.action: The pipeline advancer forwards GitHub installs that start outside a pipeline (FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR list inlined)
contracts.before_after: Same behaviour; only the list became an inline comparison.

summary: The PR adds a GitHub OAuth step before installation and checks that the logged-in GitHub user is the one who installed the app. Three problems need fixing. First, the installer check reads `metadata["sender"]` without a guard; Integrations created through the pipeline never store a sender, so reinstalling one fails with a 500. Second, errors from the token exchange and from `get_user_info` are not caught, so they also become a 500 instead of the error page. Third, `test_installation_not_found` now fails at the state check and no longer tests the not-found path. To consider: the installer check does not run when the webhook has not created the Integration yet, and `redirect_uri` is not URL-encoded.
